observations: A large rounded head fills most of the grey field; heavy black outlines define the skull shape while leaving the interior open to layered color patches of yellow-green, purple, red, and teal.
The eye socket area is dominated by a dark maroon rectangular form with white highlights inside, creating a hollow, mask-like cavity at the center of the composition.
The lower face opens into a wide gap crossed by dense vertical black hatching, with magenta, teal, and red lines scrawling across the chin and neck below.
reading: The grey ground holds the head at a slight downward tilt, giving the figure a lowered, weighted presence. Color patches—yellow-green across the crown, purple along the jaw, teal at the collar—sit beneath the black scaffolding rather than filling it neatly. The hollow eye socket reads as absence more than feature. That open lower gap, striped with hatching, carries a rawness the tight skull outline keeps from spilling outward.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #165 and nnxyz nnotb #167. Where #165 fills its field with a flat black ground and radiating marks, #166 keeps the grey open around the figure, making the head feel more isolated. Title order and recorded creation order align here.

connections.reason: Both works place a large head on a grey ground with yellow as the dominant warm accent, but nnxyz #3 scatters marks across the full field while #166 concentrates color inside a tighter black outline, making the contrast in containment visible.

lookingQuestion: Where does the black outline hold the color patches inside the head, and where does it break or let them escape—and what does that difference do to how the face reads?
ambiguities: The scrawled signature in the lower right is consistent with other works in the owned subset but its exact lettering is not fully legible at this resolution.
nnxyz nnotb #167 shows a warm-toned animal subject on a brown ground with a very different mark density; no meaningful formal connection to #166 was found, so it was omitted.
